scope: Finite own C/H source contracts and prior cached entry text only; no compile, producer import, native binary, instruction, emulator, or device access

findings.effect: Clears active for an exact current session and retains the session high-water mark; this is packet-policy state, not endpoint retirement.
Successful path clears only music_gate_bindings[seid-1].callback after checking the original SEP is idle and matches.
findings.follow_on: Configuration dispatch without the local binding falls through to the original handler; this does not prove retirement or quiescence.

findings.effect: Publishes a callback and module-owned capability pointer. Prior native bytes are stack-local rollback data for claim failure, not a retained unregister record.
The supplied contract requires code/callback/capabilities pinned until reboot and explicitly provides no unload/unregister path.
The added bootstrap contract says later voice loads can overwrite the fixed stock DLL buffer and disclaims a loader pin/unload protocol; its phase word is reloaded on each file load.

action_changed: Do not treat gate release or policy unbind as module unloading permission. A typed owner must retain code/data lifetime, retire native endpoint publication and drain callbacks/work before replacement, or prove a supported always-pinned design.
limits: No complete candidate call graph or other generated lifecycle sources were reviewed here; this does not establish absence of an external retirement mechanism.
No actual voice replacement, concurrent callback, stop completion, hardware audio, cold boot, or loader pin was tested.
Source contract assertions are not native execution or installation validation.
